events.reason: Severe diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, fever

reports.text: Single upright frontal view of the chest. Free intraperitoneal air beneath the diaphragm. Lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Free air under the diaphragm, consistent with a perforated viscus. Findings called to the ED physician at 19:48.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 10/11/2025 18:52

CC: severe abdominal pain, nausea, fever

HPI: 59-year-old man with a history of recurrent diverticulitis, followed by his primary care practice since 2018, with hypertension, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Pain started roughly 4 hours ago, shortly after eating. At first it was sharp and severe, then let up for a short time, and is now spread across his whole abdomen and constant. Nauseated, feels feverish. No prior abdominal surgery.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, about one glass of wine nightly, postal service supervisor.
Family: father MI at 58, mother type 2 diabetes, brother hypertension.

Triage vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 102, BP 135/85.

Exam: Appears uncomfortable, lying still. Abdomen with tenderness throughout, rebound and voluntary guarding. Bowel sounds diminished.

Results: WBC 16.4 with 88% neutrophils, left shift. Upright chest film shows free air under the diaphragm.

MDM: Peritonitis with pneumoperitoneum; given his history, perforated diverticulitis is most likely. NPO, IV fluids, IV piperacillin-tazobactam, IV analgesia and antiemetic. General surgery consulted at bedside and will take him to the OR tonight.

Diagnosis: perforated diverticulitis with peritonitis.
Disposition: admitted to general surgery.

reports.text: Specimen: sigmoid colon, segmental resection. Gross: segment of sigmoid colon with multiple diverticula and a perforation site with overlying fibrinopurulent exudate. Microscopic: acute and chronic diverticulitis with perforation and acute serositis. Margins viable. Lymph nodes reactive. No dysplasia or malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Sigmoid colon: perforated diverticulitis with acute serositis. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Operative report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 10/11/2025, case start 23:40
Preoperative diagnosis: perforated viscus, suspected perforated diverticulitis
Postoperative diagnosis: perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with purulent peritonitis
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy, sigmoid colectomy with primary colorectal anastomosis, abdominal washout
Anesthesia: general endotracheal
Findings: purulent fluid throughout the abdomen from a perforated sigmoid diverticulum. No feculent contamination. Remainder of the colon and small bowel healthy in appearance.
Description: Midline laparotomy. Purulent fluid evacuated. Sigmoid mobilized, resected between staple lines to healthy, well-perfused bowel. Stapled end-to-end colorectal anastomosis, air leak test negative. Abdomen irrigated. Fascia closed, skin loosely approximated.
EBL 150 mL. No complications. To PACU in stable condition.
General surgery

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/11/2025, discharged 10/17/2025
Service: general surgery

Diagnosis: perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with purulent peritonitis
Procedure: 10/11/2025 exploratory laparotomy, sigmoid colectomy with primary anastomosis (no stoma)

Course: Taken to the OR from the ED the night of arrival. Uneventful recovery. IV piperacillin-tazobactam continued for 4 days after surgery, then stopped. Diet advanced from postoperative day 3, tolerating regular food, bowel function returned. Metformin and lisinopril held while NPO, both resumed before discharge. Blood sugars monitored in house. Pathology: perforated diverticulitis, no dysplasia or cancer. Incision clean and dry at discharge.

Discharge medications:
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (resume)
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily (resume)
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily (resume)
- acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain
- oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, 12 tablets, no refills

Allergies: NKDA
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks; call for fever, worsening abdominal pain, wound redness or drainage.
Follow-up: general surgery clinic in 2 weeks; primary care within 1-2 weeks of discharge.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know I was in the hospital last week. My diverticulitis came back bad, they said it busted through and I had emergency surgery that night, they took out part of my colon. No bag thank God. Home since Friday, sore but getting around. Can you get the paperwork from the hospital.

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm so sorry you went through that, and glad you are home and moving. We'll request the hospital records today. I'd like to see you in the next week or two to look at the incision and go over your diabetes and blood pressure meds; please call the front desk to set that up. Call right away or go back to the ED for fever, worse belly pain, vomiting, or redness or drainage at the incision.

documents.title: Your hospital records
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Coleman, your hospital records finally arrived and I've read through them. The pathology showed inflammation from the diverticulitis and no cancer, which is good news. I still haven't seen you since September of last year and want to check on your recovery, your diabetes and your blood pressure. Please call us to schedule; we have early morning openings.
